datasets.title: PSA 2020 census geography
datasets.geography: Philippines, Region XII, South Cotabato, Koronadal City
datasets.description: Official 1 May 2020 population for the country, SOCCSKSARGEN, South Cotabato, and Koronadal City.
datasets.source_note: National total from PSA Proclamation coverage of the 2020 CPH. Region XII and South Cotabato household counts from PSA RSSO XII Special Release 2022-SR-R1263-002. Koronadal city total from the same census as compiled by PhilAtlas from PSA tables.

records.name: Koronadal City
records.role: Provincial capital and SOCCSKSARGEN regional center

datasets.title: Koronadal barangay population
datasets.description: 2020 census population for all 27 Koronadal barangays, used to turn raw referral counts into cases per 1,000 residents.
datasets.source_note: Barangay counts are the PSA 2020 Census figures published for Koronadal. Saravia and Topland are the local names used by CareLink for the PSA barangays Sarabia and Zulueta.

datasets.title: Koronadal age structure
datasets.description: 2015 census age groups for Koronadal, used as the local baseline for child, working-age, and senior share.
datasets.source_note: Age distribution is from the 2015 Census (total 174,942). The 2020 census did not publish this age split on the same city profile.

datasets.title: South Cotabato city and municipal population
datasets.description: 2020 population of Koronadal and the 10 municipalities, so city referrals can be read against the rest of the province.
datasets.source_note: PSA 2020 CPH. General Santos is a highly urbanized city and is not part of this provincial total.

datasets.title: South Cotabato primary care facilities
datasets.publisher: South Cotabato Province-Wide Health System and Referral Manual
datasets.description: Provincial facility counts that frame barangay-to-city referral load.
datasets.source_note: Facility counts are from the provincial referral manual (facility mapping and the RHU/BHS table). Population figures in that manual are a later projection; CareLink uses the PSA 2020 census for population.

records.note: Lake Sebu is the RHU without its own birthing facility; an infirmary sits beside that RHU.

datasets.title: DOH primary care programs
datasets.description: DOH programs a barangay health station or city health office is expected to deliver or refer.
datasets.source_note: Program names follow current DOH national programs. Keyword lists are used only to match CareLink referral reasons to the right program.

records.name: PhilPEN noncommunicable disease package
records.action: Keep antihypertensive and diabetes follow-up inside the city NCD clinic before cases become emergencies.

records.name: Maternal, newborn, and child health and nutrition
records.action: Protect prenatal and postpartum slots at the city health office and birthing facility.

records.name: National Tuberculosis Program (TB-DOTS)
records.action: Route symptomatic patients to TB-DOTS screening instead of a general queue.

records.name: National Immunization Program
records.action: Separate catch-up immunization from curative referrals so vaccine sessions are not crowded out.

records.name: National Dengue Prevention and Control Program
records.action: Apply the 4S advisory: search and destroy breeding sites, seek early consultation, self-protection, and fogging only when indicated.

records.name: National Rabies Prevention and Control Program
records.action: Send animal-bite cases to a bite treatment center the same day.

records.name: Integrated Management of Childhood Illness
records.action: Screen under-five referrals with IMCI and nutrition follow-up before specialist referral.

records.name: Mental Health Act service pathway
records.action: Keep a mental health counseling slot so these referrals are not left in the general queue.

records.name: Family planning program
records.action: Offer method refill at the barangay or city clinic without a specialist referral.

records.name: Oral health program
records.action: Batch dental referrals toward the city oral health clinic.

records.name: Acute respiratory infection care
records.action: Stock inhalers and pediatric respiratory assessment, matching the country's leading cause of morbidity.

datasets.title: PIDSR notifiable diseases
datasets.description: Diseases the Philippine Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response system expects facilities to report.
datasets.source_note: Category labels follow the DOH PIDSR disease list used by epidemiology and surveillance units. A match means the referral text should be checked for reporting, not that a case is confirmed.

datasets.title: SOCCSKSARGEN leading morbidity, December 2025
datasets.description: December 2025 FHSIS causes for the region CareLink serves. Compared with live referral text only when the same condition appears.
datasets.source_note: DOH Epidemiology Bureau, FHSIS CY 2025 December Monthly Report, Region XII table, as of 11 February 2026. The report says these figures are partial.

datasets.title: Philippine seasonal health calendar
datasets.publisher: PAGASA climate types and Department of Health seasonal advisories
datasets.geography: Philippines, with a Koronadal Type IV note
datasets.description: Months when dengue, leptospirosis, diarrhea, respiratory illness, and heat illness usually rise.
datasets.source_note: National rainy season is June to November and the hot dry season is March to May. South Cotabato is generally PAGASA Climate Type IV, so rain is more evenly spread and these diseases can appear outside the national peak.

records.guidance: Search and destroy mosquito breeding sites and fast-track fever referrals.
Ask about flood exposure when fever follows heavy rain.
Check safe-water advice and oral rehydration at the barangay station.
Separate respiratory cough cases from routine wellness visits.
Watch dehydration during the hot months, including outdoor workers and seniors.

datasets.title: South Cotabato indigenous peoples
datasets.description: Indigenous groups CareLink should recognize when a patient is tagged as indigenous.
datasets.source_note: T'boli, B'laan, and Manobo are the principal indigenous groups associated with South Cotabato. Lake Sebu and T'boli municipality are the main ancestral domains; Koronadal also serves IP patients referred into the city.

datasets.title: Priority population laws
datasets.description: Statutes that match CareLink patient tags: senior, PWD, solo parent, indigenous, pregnant, and child.
datasets.source_note: Used so AI recommendations name the law behind a priority tag. These are eligibility and service-priority rules, not clinical diagnoses.

records.name: Universal Health Care Act
records.action: Check PhilHealth Konsulta eligibility before a paid specialist step.

records.name: Expanded Senior Citizens Act
records.action: Keep a senior lane for chronic-care follow-up.

records.name: Magna Carta for Disabled Persons
records.action: Do not leave PWD referrals in a standing queue.

records.name: Expanded Solo Parents Welfare Act
records.action: Offer a shorter return visit when the caregiver is a solo parent.

records.name: Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act
records.action: Record indigenous identity only for service access, and involve the city IP desk when language is a barrier.

records.name: Mental Health Act
records.action: Mental health referrals need a named counseling pathway.

records.name: Responsible Parenthood and Reproductive Health Act
records.action: Keep family planning and prenatal services available at the referring center.

datasets.title: DOH service delivery network
datasets.description: The referral ladder from a barangay health station up to an apex hospital. This is the pathway CareLink automates inside Koronadal.
datasets.source_note: Levels follow the DOH service delivery network used by provincial health systems: barangay health station, rural health unit or city health office, then hospital.

records.role: First contact, prevention, and upward referral.

records.facility: Rural Health Unit or City Health Office
records.role: Primary care, prenatal care, TB-DOTS, immunization, and hospital referral.
